text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
NASA BORBA

- The Serbian government suspends work of muncipal authorities in Novi Pazar, in the predominantly Moslem Sandzak area, and appoints a council to take over their duties. All access roads to town blocked by police on Thursday and police presence intensified.

- Serbian committee for relations with Serbs outside Serbia expressed concern over the killing of former Bosnian Serb police chief Simo Drljaca and called for an urgent investigation into the incident.
- The opposition Democratic Party submitted over 1,600 amendments to the electoral laws on the agenda of the third extraordinary Serbian parliament session.

- The ruling Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) will submit the candidacy of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic as new Yugoslav President at the upcoming federal parliament session and expects the Montenegrin socialists will honour the decision of their main board to support this, an SPS spokesman said.

- Opposition Democratic Party (DS) and Civic Alliance Party (GSS) writes letter to OSCE complaining over uncertain electoral conditions in Serbia, partiality of state media and the draft of the local self-government law.
- Assembly of Yugoslav association of agricultural producers Jugoagrar asks for adoption of a law turning short-term farm credits to a public debt.
- Italian firm Italgas is working on a 670 million Italian lira feasibility study for a gas network in Serbian towns.
- Former Belgrade Mayor Nebojsa Covic is going to set up a new party called the Democratic Alternative.
- Trial of 15 ethnic Albanians charged of terrorist action ended in Pristina district court on Thursday, the court to pronounce sentences on Friday.
POLITIKA

- The Serbian Development Fund extended the first credits to exporting firms from the close to $1 million obtained from the sale of a 49 percent stake in Serbia's telecom company. The total value of the credits is 126 million German marks extended to 45 exporters and range individually from 250,000 to 10 million marks.
- Yugoslavia-Macedonia border talks continued in Belgrade an inter-state agreement expected to be reached shortly.
- Zastava cars is returning to Polish markets, will export 1,000 Yugos for assembly by end of year.
- Conditions exist to maintain the stability of the dinar and the prices with the economic and monetary policy measures, says National Bank of Yugoslavia board of governors.
- Delegation of Germany's Siemens discussing future projects with Serbian power industry Elektroprivreda Srbije and railways.
- The SFOR action in Bosnia is an action of an occupation army and not peace troops, said spokesman of the Yugoslav Left (JUL), member of the ruling coalition.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Yugoslav beef not expected to head to European markets until after necessary EU checks which will not be before September.
DANAS

- Prijedor mayor Milomir Stakic denies SFOR version that former Bosnian Serb police chief Simo Drljaca was killed in self-defence says there is an eyewitness report Drljaca was shot on the banks of a lake where he was fishing.
DNEVNI TELEGRAF

- Former Bosnian Serb commander and indicted war criminal general Ratko Mladic quoted by the paper's source to have said: "I am not going anywhere from here alive, I am a general of the Yugoslav army," when Montenegrin police tried to expell him from the republic.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --

- The main board of the Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) to decide on its candidate for the republic's president from a five member list. Parliament speaker Svetozar Marovic withdraws his name from the list in favour of Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic.

- The Montenegrin government and the Friedrich Ebert foundation signed a cooperation agreement; the foundation will open offices in Podgorica shortly to support economic, social and scientific projects.

- The Montenegrin Information ministry rejected as untrue President Momir Bulatovic's allegations that import-export firm ASI has an outstanding tax debt of 40 million dinars. ASI issued its own press release confirming it paid all taxes.
- There are 23,000 tourists in Budva, up 11 percent on the same period last year.
-- Belgrade newsroom 381 11 311 4305
